summary: The contract is coherent and fully candidate-visible. The verifier grades each plan with a byte-identical copy of the shipped /app/tools/check_plan.py (the manifest hashes match) and with day files whose roster SHA-256 values equal the shipped /app/days/*.json hashes. It applies the documented pass rule cost <= target from targets.json, which is also identical to the shipped copy. Output paths, file format, validity rules, cost formula and parse limits in stand-rules.md agree with the checker. No hidden rule, tie-break, representation constraint or contradiction was found.
checks_performed: Compared packet-manifest hashes: environment/app/tools/check_plan.py and tests/check_plan.py are identical (603464e7...). environment/app/days/targets.json and tests/targets.json are identical (b97e3aa0...).

Compared each tests/days/roster.json sha256 with the manifest hash of environment/app/days/day-N.json. All four match, and tests/test_outputs.py:36 asserts that the decompressed verifier copy has this hash, so the verifier grades exactly the candidate-visible days. The .json.gz files are binary and were not decompressed. Their equivalence rests on that hash assertion.

Mapped the instruction's output path /app/plans/<day>.json (instruction.md:1) to the verifier's PLANS default /app/plans plus name.json (tests/test_outputs.py:21,44). They agree for day-1 through day-4.
Mapped the pass rule 'costs no more than the day's target' (instruction.md:1) to cost <= TARGETS[name] (tests/test_outputs.py:55).

Traced each stand-rules.md validity rule to check_plan.py. Coverage (placed exactly once, known stand, string turn ids) maps to lines 83-96. Size and international rules map to lines 103-106. The buffer rule maps to lines 107-110. Wingtip rules map to lines 112-118.

Proved statically that the consecutive-after-sort buffer check matches the pairwise rule 3. Sorting by arrive means d1+b<=a2<=a3, so no non-consecutive pair can conflict. With depart >= arrive, equal arrivals are always rejected, as the rule requires.
Traced the cost formula in stand-rules.md:48-59 (remote bus charge per turn, walk_metres list-index lookup with a nonzero diagonal, no other charges) to check_plan.py:120-131.

Traced the file-format limits in stand-rules.md:61-74 to check_plan.py:17-73: the byte cap, digit cap, BOM/NaN/Infinity rejection, duplicate-name rejection, depth 64 counting the top level as 1, ignored extra top-level keys, and omitted or empty stands allowed.

Ran a regex scan over all four day files for decimal literals and found none, so the documented claim 'Costs are whole numbers' holds for the integer data. Every day has buffer_minutes 15 and bus_cost_per_passenger 300.

Sampled the structure of day-1 and day-4 (stands list with R stands last, walk_metres matrix with a nonzero diagonal of 40, wingtip_pairs, turns, transfers). It matches the field definitions in stand-rules.md:8-29.
Checked the instruction's environment claims (no network, nothing installable, Python 3.13 stdlib) against environment/Dockerfile and task.toml [agent] network_mode no-network.
Checked the README usage lines against the actual tool signatures (DAY.json PLAN.json).

coverage_sweep.category: Every grading rule has a candidate-visible authoritative source
coverage_sweep.reason: The verifier applies only load_plan/evaluate from a byte-identical copy of the shipped checker, plus cost <= target from an identical copy of the targets. stand-rules.md declares that it states the rules the checker applies, and the instruction points to both files. No verifier-only rule exists.

coverage_sweep.category: Input domain and boundaries the task needs (buffer equality, wingtip strictness, size/international, file limits)
coverage_sweep.reason: Buffer equality is allowed ('no later than', checked as d1+buffer > a2). Wingtip overlap is strict with no buffer. Size 'at most' and the international-only restriction are explicit. The byte, digit and depth limits are stated with inclusive semantics that match the code.

coverage_sweep.category: Rendered instruction, declared artifacts and verifier output paths agree
coverage_sweep.reason: The instruction names /app/plans/<day>.json for four days. task.toml declares artifacts /app/plans/. The verifier reads /app/plans/day-N.json. There is no broken template text or sentinel.

coverage_sweep.category: Examples and supporting artifacts support the stated rules
coverage_sweep.reason: The format example in stand-rules.md matches the checker's expected shape. The README commands match the tool usage. The shipped planner implements the same buffer and wingtip semantics. Its output is not graded.

coverage_sweep.category: Conflicting sources of truth (candidate days/targets vs verifier copies)
coverage_sweep.reason: The verifier's days are hash-bound to the candidate-visible days through the roster. The targets and the checker are byte-identical.
The plan is parsed as JSON. Turn order within a stand list is explicitly free ('in any order'), stands may be omitted, and extra top-level keys are ignored. No byte-level comparison is made.

The instruction states each target is the cost of an existing best-found plan. Standard-library Python is enough to write valid plans, and the checker is available locally. No requirement contradicts another. How hard the targets are to reach is a difficulty question, not a contract defect.

interaction_sweep.case_or_path: Two size-3 turns on the neighbouring stands of a wingtip pair, where one departs exactly as the other arrives. The wingtip rule uses strict overlap with no buffer, so they do not clash. The per-stand buffer applies only within one stand. Docs and checker agree.
A transfer between two turns on remote stands pays both turns' bus charges plus the walk entry. The docs state this explicitly, and the checker sums both independently.

A candidate could confuse the pier 'position' field with the list index. The docs name the list index explicitly ('position i of the stands list'), and the checker uses enumerate order, so the rule is disclosed.
When a wingtip-pair stand is omitted from the plan, the checker uses .get(a, []), so no error occurs. This is consistent with the rule that a stand may be left out.
A duplicate turn across two stands, a non-string turn id, or an unknown stand id is rejected. Each follows from 'every turn on exactly one stand' and 'ids exactly as in the day file'.
